system.name: Harmonic
system.one_liner: a hardware-assisted RDMA performance isolation system for public clouds that intercepts RDMA control verbs at the kernel driver

components.name: (1) Bare-metal
components.role: scheme where the tenant instance has full, direct hardware access with no host virtualization layer; not considered by Harmonic since isolation is unnecessary here

components.name: Userspace Libraries
components.role: tenant-owned userspace RDMA library issuing verbs to the driver

components.name: Drivers
components.role: tenant-owned driver issuing control/data verbs directly to the NIC

components.name: (2) Containerize Cloud
components.role: scheme where a containerized tenant's control verbs pass through a cloud-owned host driver; Harmonic's prototype focus

components.role: scheme where a hypervisor mediates a VM tenant's control verbs, with SR-IOV allowing some to bypass it directly

content.key_idea: RDMA control verbs can be intercepted at four different points depending on the virtualization scheme (bare-metal, containerized, guest VM with SR-IOV, or microkernel daemon); Harmonic needs driver-level interception, which holds for scenarios (2)-(4) but not bare-metal.

summary: This background figure catalogs four RDMA virtualization schemes that Harmonic considers for intercepting control verbs. Each scheme is drawn as a small Tenant/Host/NIC stack: (1) Bare-metal, where the tenant's own driver talks directly to NIC firmware/ASIC with no isolation boundary; (2) Containerize Cloud, where a cloud-owned host driver mediates the tenant's control verbs; (3) Guest Virtual Machine, where a hypervisor mediates control verbs but SR-IOV lets some bypass it directly to the NIC; and (4) Microkernel Approach, where a privileged host daemon mediates control verbs. A shared legend colors boxes by ownership (tenant software, cloud software, cloud hardware) and distinguishes red control-verb arrows (solid or SR-IOV-dashed) from purple data-verb arrows. Harmonic targets schemes (2)-(4), where the cloud provider can intercept control verbs at the driver/hypervisor/daemon layer, excluding bare-metal where such interception is unnecessary.

notes: The measured index records this figure as a single panel, but it visually presents four side-by-side scheme variants sharing one legend; treated here as a matrix of four comparable mini-diagrams.
